title: Step P6: one independent hand-worked example of a first building option, written into the R6B reference cases: whether a building may be lower than the minimum base height; a footprint and floors worked by hand for a made-up interior lot and for the recorded corner lot (lot coverage by portion; variants where a property fact is missing); what a floor schedule must list; the arithmetic of the preliminary apartment estimate on the owner's starting values, kept apart from the legal ceiling; reference rows and worked examples only: NO rule file, NO engine code, NO result, NO capture, NO register entry, NO human verdict [handoff seq 152 item 2; D-090 R291, R519, R545, R650, R651, R664, R686 to R690, R699, R700]
objective: Write the two independent readings of step P6 into the R6B reference cases as a new step-P6 case: one hand-worked example of a FIRST BUILDING OPTION. No reference case works a building option, a floor stack or a floor schedule by hand (row real-lot#L15 says so), and one point of law that a first building turns on was captured but never read independently: whether a building may be lower than the minimum base height. The list of the readings that are necessary, and of the earlier readings that are NOT repeated, is quoted in the G0 report. INPUT MADE BY THE ORCHESTRATOR BEFORE THE BUILDER STARTS: two readings by two different AI helpers that took no part in writing the program's rules, each working alone from a sealed folder (all 185 pinned law captures without their notes; the benchmark lot's recorded official facts and outline; one made-up interior lot of 100 ft by 100 ft in plain R6B with every fact stated; 34 answers settled by earlier readings, copied word for word from the reference cases and given as settled, so that completed readings are reused and not worked again; and three starting values chosen by the owner, marked as assumptions), with no access to the program, the repository or the web. Both answer the same eight questions (Q1 to Q8). STEP 1: save the two returns unchanged under docs/reference-cases/R6B/provenance/ as return-independent-hand-calculation-13.md and return-independent-hand-calculation-14.md, each with a short header in the words of the headers of files 11 and 12, and pin each file's digest. STEP 2: write the step-P6 reading into docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/step-p6-worked.json (and its rendered page step-p6-worked.md), following the form of cases/step-p5-worked.json, with rows for: (1) THE MINIMUM BASE HEIGHT: whether a new building whose whole height is below the minimum base height is permitted in plain R6B and in a C2-2 overlay mapped within R6B, by which words (ZR 23-431, 23-432, 23-436, 35-631, 35-632, 35-633 as the readings quote them), every condition the words attach, what the street-wall words then require of such a building, and whether any captured provision sets a least height or a least number of storeys; (2) THE MADE-UP LOT: the front, side and rear yards for an interior lot 100 ft wide in plain R6B; where the street wall must or may stand given the stated neighbours; the footprint of the widest building with the limit that binds each edge; building A storey by storey (plan, floor area, running total, height of each storey's top), its total against the maximum with the floor area left unused, its height against the minimum base height, the maximum base height and the maximum building height; building B the same; (3) WHAT A FLOOR SCHEDULE MUST LIST so that a reader can check such a building against each limit; (4) THE REAL LOT: the lot coverage BY PORTION (the words that divide the lot; the sides and area of the corner-lot portion and of the rest as each reading measured them; the area of building each allows; the total); the variants of the rear yard beyond the corner area, each with the missing fact that would select it; where the street wall must or may stand, with every missing fact; what the missing ground elevations leave open; the footprint of building A under each variant; buildings A and B under each variant; and which figures are the same under every variant; (5) THE ARITHMETIC OF THE PRELIMINARY APARTMENT ESTIMATE for every building worked: the residential floor area the building holds, times 0.60 and times 0.75, divided by 700, to two decimals, with the whole numbers just below and above; and SEPARATELY the legal ceiling on dwelling units for each lot; (6) what both readers did not have, the missing facts about the real lot, and every settled answer a reader found a text to contradict. THE RULE OF AGREEMENT: record a value or a yes/no ONLY where BOTH readings give it on the same basis (same facts, same quoted words, same route, and for a figure the same number to the precision the row states); everywhere else record 'not known' or 'not sure' with the reason, both readings named and what each says, and what would settle it. Where one reading attaches a condition the other does not, state that condition in the value. The builder does not pick a winner and adds no reading of its own. THE KIND OF EVERY GAP (owner row R650): every row that stays not known says which kind its gap is: a missing fact about the property (name the fact and where it would come from), or unresolved law (the captured text does not settle it, or the readers did not have a text: name it). 'Code not built' is never a reason in a case: a case holds nothing about the program. WHAT THE EXAMPLE IS AND IS NOT: both buildings are a plain stack (every storey the same plan), by a fixed method that the orchestrator's brief gave the readers. Say in the case's summary and in each building row that this shape is the METHOD OF THE EXAMPLE, an assumption, not a rule of law, not the owner's decision and not a recommendation of what to build; that both buildings stay at or below the maximum base height, so no storey above the base is counted (owner row R519); and that the floor-to-floor height of 10 ft, the share range 0.60 to 0.75 and the apartment size of 700 sq ft are STARTING ASSUMPTIONS CHOSEN BY THE OWNER, not validated, not measured and not law, and that the made-up lot describes no real property: the example checks a method (owner row R545). The estimate's figures are arithmetic on those assumptions; they are kept in rows of their own, apart from every legal limit, and never rounded to a count (no rounding rule was given). THE SIX STEPS OF THE COMPLETE CALCULATION (owner rows R687, R688, R690): the owner asks that, for the first building option, an independently worked example be compared with the program's actual output through the complete calculation: the property inputs; the footprint; each floor's area and height; the total floor area; the applicable legal unit limit; the separate preliminary apartment estimate. THIS TASK MAKES THE INDEPENDENT SIDE of that comparison and nothing of the program's side (a case holds nothing from a program run; the program's side and the comparison itself are the next task's, in the zoning-rule review register). So, for each lot and each building worked, the case carries all six steps as rows that a later comparison can read one by one, and each building row and each estimate row carries its figures ALSO AS NUMBERS in a structured block (the property inputs used; the footprint's sides and area; one entry per storey with its floor-to-floor height, the height of its top, its plan area and its floor area; the total floor area and the floor area left unused; the legal unit limit; the estimate's floor area, share range, apartment size, two quotients and the whole numbers below and above), added to the row shape with the fewest changes and shown by the renderer; the tests recompute from that block. Where the two readings differ on a figure the block holds both, named, and no single figure. The legal unit limit and the estimate are separate rows with separate sources. At the end one row lists every step on which the two readings differ and every missing fact, each with its kind and what would settle it. LEGAL REQUIREMENT OR DESIGN ASSUMPTION (owner rows R699, R700): every figure and every step in a building row or an estimate row is marked as one of two things: a LEGAL REQUIREMENT (with its quoted text) or a CHOSEN DESIGN ASSUMPTION (the same-plan stack, the floor-to-floor height, the place of a plan on the lot where the law leaves it free, the share range, the apartment size). The apartment size of 700 sq ft and the share range 0.60 to 0.75 are labelled, in these words, 'preliminary assumption' wherever they appear. ONE CURRENT ANSWER PER QUESTION: where a new row gives the current answer to a question an older row holds, mark the older row superseded_by the new row with a dated change-log entry; never leave two current answers. Known candidates, to decide by the rule and list in the report: cases/real-lot.json row L15 (building option, floor plates, floors: not known because no independent worked example exists) and row L5 (maximum lot coverage: not known), and cases/corner-reach.json row real-lot-coverage (no single whole-lot figure; read per portion). The whole-lot coverage rows keep their kind and value text exactly unless BOTH readings work the two portions of that lot to the same areas. THE REACH ROWS of cases/corner-reach.json (real-lot-reach, C1-reach, C2-reach, C3-reach) are read by other tasks' tests: do not change, reword or supersede them. An existing row's expected value or kind changes ONLY where both new readings support the change on the same basis, with a dated change-log entry. Say 'the readers did not have' a text outside their folder and 'not read by reading N' for a text in the folder a reader chose not to read; never 'not captured'. Update docs/reference-cases/R6B/README.md with a step-P6 section and its 'did not have' list; re-render the pages; extend the test support only as the new rows need (new modules r6b_reference_cases_step_p6.py and test_r6b_reference_cases_step_p6.py, modelled on the step-P5 pair; add 'step-p6-worked' to r6b_reference_cases_lib.py CASE_IDS and REQUIRED_BASE_IDS and wire the step-P6 guards into r6b_reference_cases_check.py; r6b_reference_cases_render.py only if a new row shape needs it). THE OWNER'S STANDARDS this reading carries: every statement of what the law says quotes the captured text with its file and content digest; the reading is labelled an unreviewed draft with a link to the source text; where the text does not settle a point the reading says 'not sure' and names what would settle it; a missing fact stays unknown and is never replaced by a default; legal limits are kept apart from practical estimates; a question of law is never turned into the owner's preference; and each worked example is worked by hand from the text, not matched to a program run. THE ZONING-RULE REVIEW REGISTER: this task changes no rule and no calculation of the program, so it moves no register entry (owner row R691 asks for the register to move with every change of a rule or a calculation: there is none here). The register's page for the first building option, with this case as its worked example and expected answer beside the program's actual answer, is the next task's. No human verdict is entered anywhere. TESTS REQUIRED: one acceptance test per input state, with a table in the producer report; the arithmetic of every worked row is re-computed by a test from the row's own stated inputs (each storey table sums to its total; total plus unused equals the maximum; plan area times storeys equals the building's floor area; the estimate's four figures follow from the floor area the building holds) so that a changed figure is caught; a red proof that a changed reading is caught; and one mutation proof per pinned branch (a not-known row given a value is refused; a value where the two readings differ is refused; an estimate row that calls its figures a count, a limit or validated is refused; the superseded rows stay superseded and the new targets current). NOT IN THIS TASK: any program code (the lot coverage by portion, the building option's generator, the floor schedule, the estimator are later tasks that will be tested against this case); the results document, the screen and every fixture; the measurement-basis record; any rule file, capture, register entry or plan; and entering a human verdict anywhere.
business_reason: The owner's order after the bounded fixes is the first building shape, the floor schedule and the preliminary apartment estimate, by the smallest remaining work (rows R663, R664), with independently worked, source-backed examples to check interpretation (row R291; matching the program's own saved output is not proof). The results document withholds the building option today for two reasons that this case addresses: the sample building is below the minimum base height and no independently worked example of a building option exists. Until the case exists, no generator, floor schedule or estimator can be tested against anything but itself.

The example's shape or the owner's starting values read as law, as validated or as a recommendation -> the summary and each building and estimate row say what they are (S3, S9); a guard refuses the words
A variant for a missing fact read as the answer -> each variant names its missing fact; the rear yard beyond the corner area stays not known (S7, S8)
A figure recorded where the two readings differ in the second decimal or in the measured sides -> the rule of agreement states the precision; both figures are given (S6, S12)
Two current answers for one question -> the older row is superseded with a dated entry (S12)
Growing the main test module past its size -> the step-P6 rows and tests go into new focused modules
